title: The Relationship between Screen Time Duration and Non-Verbal Imagination in Preschoolers from Different Regions of Russia
abstract: The involvement of modern preschoolers in the digital environment raises the question of how different forms of screen activity affect the development of higher mental functions, including imagination. The inconsistency of existing findings indicates the need to move from analyzing total screen time to studying the differentiated contribution of its types while considering individual characteristics. The aim of this study was to analyze the relationship between active and passive screen time and parameters of imagination (flexibility, originality, elaboration) in preschoolers, taking into account gender and regional context. The study involved 1,670 children from preparatory groups of kindergartens (mean age 6.6 years, 51.5% girls) from three regions of Russia - Moscow, Perm Krai, and the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) - which significantly differ in the typical daily screen time. Imagination was assessed using O. M. Dyachenko's "Figure Completion" technique. Data on active and passive screen time were obtained through a parent survey. The results showed that active screen time was negatively associated with certain imagination parameters (flexibility and originality coefficient), and these effects were significant only for boys and emerged exclusively in regions with low and medium screen time load. Passive screen time showed no consistent associations with imagination. The findings highlight the need for a differentiated approach to analyzing a child's digital experience, taking into account the type of activity, gender, and regional context. The results contribute to understanding the non-linear and mediated nature of the influence of the digital environment on imagination development in preschool age.
